ranking.note: Remotely triggerable memory-exhaustion vector with a measured 28x accounting gap; strongest attack-resistance item in the category.
Raised to P1: same exploitable 1p1c relay-liveness class as #36437, which it depends on, and fixes several further holes; cannot sit below its prerequisite's peers.
Moved up: peer-selection bias inside addrman buckets bears directly on eclipse resistance, the category's first-order concern.
Moved up: reviewer telemetry confirms real addrman pollution and daily failed connections, stronger evidence than neighbouring P2s.
Raised from P3: bounding crafted-witness memory (112MB->4MB) plus ~10x deserialization speedup is a DoS+performance gain comparable to other P2s, and its solo reason text did not match the card.
Moved up: closes an actual evasion of inbound relay capacity limits, ranked with the other DoS-accounting fixes.
Moved up to sit with the other DoS-protection items; removes drift in a defense that degrades with every release.
Moved down: large measured relay speedup but no correctness or attack-resistance consequence, so it sits below the DoS and sync-liveness fixes.
Moved down: responsiveness gain is substantial but author-measured only and architectural; below concrete attack/liveness fixes.
Moved up: wrongly purging reachable addresses on one network degrades peer diversity, same family as #36449/#35578.
Moved down: overlaps #34533 on the same privatebroadcast rebroadcast leak and is the narrower of the two approaches.
Moved down: loss affects only opt-in private-broadcast users across a restart, less consequential than the relay and addrman fixes above.
Moved down: opt-in hardening option for operators rather than a fix to an existing failure mode.
Moved down: a long-horizon protocol upgrade whose bandwidth and eclipse benefits only land once carved into reviewable pieces; delay carries no immediate risk.
Moved up: measured ~9x gain plus it unblocks the witnessless assumevalid sync work (#36476), unlike the other P3 items near it.
Moved up: addrman accounting correctness outranks the test-only and cosmetic P3 items it was scored beside.
Moved up to sit with the other message-handling correctness/DoS edge cases (#35936, #35321).
Moved up to sit with the other message-handling correctness/DoS edge cases.
Moved up to sit with the other misbehaviour-accounting fixes rather than below feature and tracing work.
Moved down slightly: user-visible but limited to operators toggling networkactive off.
Moved up to sit with the other Tor startup/connectivity fixes; it blocks onion service creation outright for affected operators.
Demoted to P3 for consistency with the other net/net_processing split refactors (#35040, #34824, #35561): payoff cited is modularity and speculative reuse, with no hazard retired or measured gain.
Moved down to sit with the rest of the net/net_processing refactor family, which it matches in consequence.
Demoted to P2->P3: the importance of in-band snapshot sharing is asserted by the author but disputed at the concept level by multiple contributors, so it ranks with speculative features.
Observability only; placed below the behavioural P3 fixes.

Moved up: it is a real (if narrow) duplicate-connection/log bug, ranking above test-only changes.

inconsistencies: #34533 and #36330 address the same leak (wallet rebroadcast defeating -privatebroadcast) with contradictory designs: route rebroadcasts through private broadcast vs. suppress resubmission entirely. A direction decision is needed before either merges; review #34533 first as the broader one.

Chain: #36506 explicitly depends on #36437 and re-implements part of it (reassigning orphan reconsideration on announcer erasure). Review #36437 first; #36506 should be re-read against whatever lands.

#36486 (skip ForgetTxHash for non-witness reconsiderable txs) overlaps the 'typed forgetting in TxRequestTracker' / txid==wtxid hole in #36506. Same bug class, two fixes; decide which subsumes the other.

#36015 (serialize orphanage entries) and #36521 (serialize CScriptWitness) both bound witness-induced memory blowup; #36521 may make part of #36015's accounting argument moot. They should be reviewed with each other in mind.
#35558 is stacked on open PR #35724, which is not in this list; its review order is constrained by a dependency outside the category.

Private-broadcast cluster all builds on merged #29415: #34271 is leftover review feedback from that merge, while #34322, #36358, #36477, #34533 and #36330 extend it. #34271 duplicates already-merged work's cleanup and has no claim on review time.
net/net_processing split family (#30988, #35040, #34824, #35561, #35502, #35522) will conflict with each other; #35522 was resurfaced during review of #34824, so #34824 should go first.
#36244 and #36445 both reduce cs_main contention in the message loop; #36445 is the self-contained subset and should be reviewed first, then re-checked against #36244.

Tor-area PRs #36142, #36170, #36177 and #36374 all touch torcontrol/proxy parsing and will conflict; #36142 and #36170 change startup behaviour and should be sequenced before the smaller #36177/#36374 fixes.

The vacuous-test repairs (#36405, #36406, #36407, #36410, #36422, #36438, #36470) are independent of one another but all correct assertions that currently pass unconditionally; they are of equal consequence and should not be spread across bands.
result.notes: This category holds an unusually large block of genuine attack-resistance and relay-liveness fixes, so P2 is wide by design; the P1 set is restricted to remotely exploitable resource exhaustion, exploitable relay-liveness holes, a privacy break that negates an opt-in feature, and an encoding memory-safety bug. The biggest consistency correction was the refactor family: #30988 was pulled down to join #35040/#34824/#35561 at P3, since all four are modularity work with no hazard retired, while #36521 was pulled up to P2 because its stated effect (bounded witness memory, 10x deserialization) matches other P2 DoS/performance work rather than P3.
